## Key finding r9: an exact bitmap BF probe is ~2x cheaper than a hashed BF probe

## Key finding r8: perfect HJ build was serial (fixed in E0024)
- E0024 follow-ups: q13 RIGHT perfect join found-match flush is still serial (small). An exact bitmap from the perfect HJ for 50-99% dense INNER builds is useless for q14 (100% dense).

## Large perfect HA (E0009/E0013): q13 -20% real but q18 +8% beyond noise each time
- The q18 plan does not change (26-bit agg stays a hash agg). The likely cause is process state left by q13's big mmap tables (page faults or the allocator) affecting q18. A retry would need to address that: reuse the buffer, or free into the buffer pool. Unverified.

## Measured r7
- q13 eager aggregation as a manual rewrite: only -4%. DEAD.
- HJ build: 7.2M-row orders build ~126ns/row (q03/q05/q09). HJ prefetch gave no gain (prior run).
- q05 HJ l_orderkey=o_orderkey: 0.34-0.39s CPU for a 455k build + 2M probe.
- dbe-tool profile output looks COLD. Use the warm JSON trick.
- No PK/UNIQUE constraints in the schema.

## How to get full operator timings
- dbe-tool sql "<warm q>; <warm q>; SET enable_profiling='json'; SET profiling_output='/home/shresth/dev/db_evolve/work/slots/slot0/.dbe/scratch_x.json'; <q>" then Grep '"operator_timing"|"operator_name"|"operator_cardinality"|"latency"|"Dynamic Filters"'. /tmp is NOT readable.
- A/B in one session: CREATE TEMP VIEW va/vb, then `from va; from vb;` x3, then profile each into a separate file.

## Key finding: CM on join keys blocks the BF
- physical_hash_join.cpp FinalizeFilters: BF only if !has_cast && no storage_offset, except an exact BF through the offset on cond 0 (E0021). A hashed BF is never pushed through an offset.
- Exact BF: TrySetExactBloomFilter (:970) caps EXACT_BF_MAX_BITS_PER_KEY=128, EXACT_BF_SMALL_RANGE=1<<22, MAX_RANGE=1<<32. Hashed BF: 12 bits/key, 4 bits in one 64-bit sector.
- PushRangeSetFilter (gap-split ranges) only for 50 < keys <= 3200.

## Measurement lessons
- The first 2-3 runs of a query in a process are slow (~2x warm-up). Alternate A/B/A/B.
- Do NOT wrap in count(*): it changes the plan. Use a temp view + `from v`.
- dbe-tool bash: no pipes, no shell variables, no $(...).
- Bench noise is ±10-20% per template (q19, q08, q03, q14 worst).
- In long bench sequences q18 is ~10% slower after q09/q13.

## Profile snapshot (r10): q18 550, q13 539, q09 464, q05 266, q03 196, q07 191, q08 186, q16 180, q04 165, q14 153, q17 146, q19 112, q22 105, q02 66. Geomean 196.9.
- q13: inner agg 3.08s CPU, orders scan 2.65s (NOT LIKE), decompress/compress 0.80s, RIGHT HJ 0.58s.
- q03: lineitem scan 2.24s CPU, HJ on l_orderkey 0.75s. The orders BF is probably exact already (~1.4M keys over 60M = 43 bits/key).
- q18: 15M-group agg dominates (exhausted).

## Dead / exhausted
- CM join-key removal, HJ prefetch, agg run-collapse, in-place finalize, FSST heap reuse, dictionary filter, scan filter cost ordering, early HT grow, sparse perfect HJ (8M range), bitpacking select, BF on sparse perfect HJ, hashed BF through CM offset, q13 eager aggregation: ~0% or worse.
- FSST DecompressVector path is not hot.

## Next candidates
1. (dispatched r10) the fused hashed probe + E0025 bundle.
2. HJ build/probe throughput on large regular builds (q05 orderkey HJ ~150ns/probe row).
3. q13: parallel found-match flush in the RIGHT perfect HJ (small); orders scan NOT LIKE 2.65s CPU.
4. MARK delim joins (IN/EXISTS in OR) via the deliminator: check the NULL semantics.
5. Large perfect HA retry, only with a fix for the q18 after-effect.

## Codebase facts
- CM: src/optimizer/compressed_materialization*. In release, CM on a join fires only if est. build >= 1M rows and join/build ratio <= 8.
- Rule order: src/optimizer/optimizer.cpp. Scan-filter cardinality: RelationStatisticsHelper::InspectTableFilter.
- Deliminator: src/optimizer/deliminator.cpp: SelectionIsReplaceableByJoinFilter (SEMI+ANTI), ConvertNotDistinctToEqual, SubqueryIsSimple.
- Join filter generation: JoinFilterPushdownOptimizer::GenerateJoinFilters. NDF conds are skipped. DELIM_GET build => build_side_has_filter.
- Perfect HJ: perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp (CanDoPerfectHashJoin, PerfectHashJoinBuildEvent since E0024). Perfect HA: plan_aggregate.cpp. FSST: src/storage/compression/fsst.cpp. BF: src/planner/filter/bloom_filter.cpp.
- Noise thresholds: q16 ~7.9%, q18 ~5%, q13 ~14%, q09 ~8.6%, q14 ~5.1%, q05 ~20%; q04 ~20%; q08/q17 ±5-15%.
- Budget is tight (~$4/session): read memory, the ledger tail and the profile head, then dispatch.

issues.title: Bundle: fused integer hashed-BF probe + exact BF up to 2^27 bits at 1024 bits/key
issues.hypothesis: In r9, A/B on q05 showed the hashed BF probe costs about 2x the exact-bitmap probe: lineitem scan 0.92s vs 0.48s CPU, wall -15%. The false-positive rows hardly mattered. The extra cost is the probe pipeline in BFTableFilter::Filter (src/planner/filter/bloom_filter.cpp:171). HashInternal slices the key vector into a dictionary vector, VectorOperations::Hash writes a hashes vector, Flatten runs, LookupHashes makes a second pass, and a third pass translates the selection. For integer keys a single fused loop can do all of it: read data[sel[i]], call duckdb::Hash<T>(v) (MurmurHash64, the same hash the build side uses), and do the bf word load and mask test. Part 2 re-lands E0025 unchanged (TrySetExactBloomFilter in physical_hash_join.cpp, middle tier range < min(2^27, count*1024)). It gave q05 -9/-18/-20% with no regressions, but missed the -20.3% bar by itself. The fused probe speeds up every BF that stays hashed: ranges above the caps, more than 1024 bits/key, and hidden templates. The exact tier covers q05.
issues.plan: 1) bloom_filter.cpp, BFTableFilter::Filter, non-exact branch: if keys_v is a FLAT_VECTOR (or DICTIONARY, via ToUnifiedFormat) of an integer physical type (INT8..INT64, UINT8..UINT64), use a new template TemplatedLookupHashed<T>. Model its loop on TemplatedLookupExact (row_sel handling, validity), but compute filter.LookupOne(Hash(static_cast<T>(data[idx]))). The hash must match what VectorOperations::Hash produces for that type. Check this in src/common/vector_operations/vector_hash.cpp: for each T, HashOp uses duckdb::Hash<T>. NULLs: copy the exact path's handling, so an invalid row is not found only when the old path would also have dropped it. The old path hashes NULL to a constant hash, so either keep that behaviour or treat NULL as found (the join filters it anyway). Decide by reading HashOp's null handling. Every other type keeps the existing HashInternal path. 2) physical_hash_join.cpp TrySetExactBloomFilter: re-apply E0025. Add a tier where range < min(1<<27, count*1024), and only multiply when count <= 2^17. Correctness: use temp tables with BIGINT and INTEGER keys plus NULLs, and a build range larger than 2^27 so the filter stays hashed. Compare results against SET disabled_optimizers='join_filter_pushdown'. Use the warm JSON profile trick to check q05 lineitem scan CPU.
issues.expected_gain: q05 -15..-20%, carried over from E0025. Any template whose BF stays hashed (sparse integer keys over a wide range) gets a 20-40% cheaper BF probe, probably q07/q08/q18/q21-like hidden joins. Visible geomean -1.5..-2.5%.
issues.generality: All runtime join BFs on integer keys, the most common join key type. The fused loop does the same work in fewer passes, so I expect no slowdowns. The 2^27 tier allocates up to 16MB per filter, only for builds of at most 128k keys at 1024 bits/key. Probes with poor locality over 16MB could miss L2 more often, but E0025 showed no regressions.
issues.risk: Low-medium. The probe hash must match the build hash bit for bit, or rows are dropped. That would show up as wrong results, which the correctness checks above catch. Read vector_hash.cpp for each type before relying on Hash<T>.
